Broaden the carve to make the ground void more legible and useful.
Increase the vertical extent of the notch so the section carries the public threshold.

graph_edits.rationale: Keep the dominant notch gesture but align it more decisively to the access-facing side so the ground threshold reads as intentional.
Widen the carved bite slightly to strengthen the public edge without destroying the primary mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass in all four views, so the basic geometry is legible and repairable. However, the dominant form is still mostly a box with a notch-like subtraction and no convincing public void or active ground seam at the verified access edge. In the views, the blue frontage is met by a sealed or neutral edge rather than a clearly opened court, undercut, or entry expression, which weakens the required neighborhood-active threshold. The silhouette is acceptable as an early massing diagram, but the section feels arbitrary for a mixed-use neighborhood-living brief: there is no strong indication of a program-bearing ground/public relationship or upper hierarchy beyond simple clipping. It therefore fails program_fit_hard_pass despite decent overall coherence.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is a taller tower-driven object; the candidate is much smaller and its current mass lacks the same public/sectional ambition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single dominant prismatic volume with a clear carved/stepped upper profile can support a mixed-use street building when the ground threshold stays legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower typology and height logic are not directly transferable to this low-rise neighborhood living brief.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A continuous vertical mass can gain character through a slight torsion/taper while preserving one main body.
